Market Cap: Find an exact contract and compare its reported valuation and liquidity. Check input freshness.
Liquidity: Compare reported pool liquidity and its timestamp. Use an external executable quote to assess an actual exit.
Liquidity vs Market Cap: Compare market cap and reported liquidity across sampled tokens; the ratio does not predict executable price impact.
Volume: Choose the exact contract and a time window. Compare observed buy/sell value and swap sizes; returned swaps are a bounded sample.
Holders: Check provider-reported holder count and top-10 concentration where available. Counts do not establish independent ownership.
Bonding Curve: Compare measured launch progress and stage coverage. Missing progress remains unknown.
Graduation: Compare confirmed graduation with unknown status and volume-only candidates. Activity alone does not confirm graduation.
DEX: Search the exact contract and compare returned pool listings, chain, and coverage before choosing a listing.
Top Holders: Check reported top-10 concentration when the provider supplies it. Research wallet roles and related addresses externally.
Accumulation: Compare buying and selling over time in the returned sample. Net buy value alone does not prove wallet accumulation.
Distribution: Look for repeated sell activity and surrounding buy flow. Establishing which holders are distributing requires external wallet history.
Supply Absorption: Compare repeated sells, subsequent buys, and price behavior in the observed window. This cannot establish buyer independence.
Organic Buying: Inspect observed buys and transaction senders as research leads. Senders can be routers; this view does not verify independent owners.
Support / Base: Find a sampled token and review its observed market history. Use Inspect's historical view or an external chart to investigate retests.
Resistance / Ceiling: Review observed price behavior and activity, then investigate repeated rejection areas in a detailed chart.
Breakout: Compare sampled price behavior, activity, and liquidity. A ranking is a research lead, not breakout confirmation.
Fake Breakout: Use historical candles where available to inspect range acceptance; buy/sell figures remain a separate bounded swap sample.
Repricing: Compare observed persistence and current liquidity in the Longer-term view. Provider history is sampled and may have gaps.
Pullback: Compare historical candle ranges and nearby observed flow. Candle volume has no directional buy/sell split.
Panic Dump: Review sell sizes and surrounding swaps for the selected listing and window. The returned sample may omit part of the event.
Entry Liquidity: Review reported liquidity as context, then obtain a current executable quote externally for the intended order.
Exit Liquidity: Review observed buying and selling as current context. Past swaps do not guarantee demand when you exit.
Narrative: Follow source evidence and confirm the exact chain and contract association; a name match alone is a lead.
Catalyst: Open the underlying source and verify the announcement with a primary source. A feed item does not confirm future demand.
Social Momentum: Inspect indexed X mentions and their evidence. RSS counts do not measure author diversity, engagement, or all X activity.
CT / KOL Shilling: Review available source posts as leads. Holdings, sponsorship, and wallet attribution require independent verification.
Attention Rotation: Compare stories and sampled activity across themes. The feed does not measure total attention or capital rotation.
Chain Narrative: Follow chain-related stories to their sources. Chain-wide user and DEX growth need separate evidence.
Meme Lifecycle: Start with observed launch stage, then compare story and market context. Launch stage is only one part of the lifecycle.
Wash Trading: Look for repetitive sizes and timing in returned swaps. These patterns are leads, not proof of wash trading.
Market Maker / Bot Activity: Review repeated trade sizes and timing. This sample does not classify bots or establish their intent.
Position Size: Use reported liquidity as context for your own risk plan. Meme Fast does not calculate a suitable position or executable exit.
Scaling Out: Review observed demand and trade sizes as exit context. Plan actual quantities and executable quotes separately.
Exit Strategy: Review changes in observed flow for an exact contract, then compare them with your written exit conditions.
Entry Liquidity vs Exit Liquidity: Compare current flow and pool coverage as context; validate intended buy and sell quantities with executable quotes elsewhere.
